data.name: Avitzur
data.gender_notes: Avitzur is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew words ‘av’ meaning ‘father’ and ‘itzchak’ meaning ‘living hew’, Avitzur translates to ‘father of hew’ or ‘bird of prey’. This name holds significance in Jewish tradition as it is the name of a legendary hero, Avitzur the Monkey-Man. The name Avitzur carries the meaning “Bird of prey” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Avitzur usually hope their child will grow to embody bird of prey and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes courage, strength, and a keen sense of observation.
data.etymology: Avitzur belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bird of prey.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Avitzur total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_english.name: Avitzur
in_english.long_meaning: The English name Avitzur is derived from the Hebrew words 'av' (father) and 'tsur' (rock or refuge), meaning 'Father of Light'. It is not commonly used as a given name in English-speaking countries.

data.cultural_impact: This name has a rich cultural impact rooted in Jewish folklore. Avitzur, meaning the ‘monkey-man’ or a bird of prey, is a powerful symbol for strength and courage; Avitzur is remembered as a hero in Jewish tradition who was saved by Noah during the great flood and was later instrumental in helping to preserve humanity by rebuilding the world post-flood. The name Avitzur is a nod to the Jewish culture's storytelling tradition and its enduring belief in the power of salvation and hope in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Avitzur holds deep spiritual significance for its emphasis on the father-child relationship and the roles they play in the cycle of life. Furthermore, the name Avitzur relates to the Jewish belief in divine providence and salvation through the symbol of being a ‘bird of prey’, representing the idea that even in the face of the unknown and danger, one can rise above it and persevere. The name serves as a reminder of the power of faith, resilience, and the strength of the bond between a father and child.
